subject: Post-discovery: dedicated capacity sizing + next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@aurorapay.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T16:12:00Z
Subject: Post-discovery: dedicated capacity sizing + next steps

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call this morning. I appreciated the walkthrough of AuroraPay's high-throughput payment reconciliation flow and the peak window details you shared. From our side the immediate next step is a dedicated sizing & technical deep-dive so we can validate throughput targets, latency SLOs, and persistence/caching constraints for a potential Dedicated pool.

Suggested agenda (30–45 min):
- Quick recap of your peak QPS and typical inference sequence lengths
- Throughput targets and latency SLOs (p95/p99 targets)
- Network and data residency constraints (ingress/egress patterns)
- Pre-call checklist & artifacts for the sizing run (we'll list below)
- Proposed slot for the deep dive + who to include from your infra team

Could you confirm the right people to invite (infra/ops + security), and share 3 windows that work next week? I can also book a 60-minute slot with Sean, our Solutions Engineer, who will run the sizing session and capture a mutual action plan.

Pre-call artifacts that would help us move faster: (we've attached a short checklist)
- 72-hour request/traffic trace or CSV of request timestamps
- Example input payloads and max sequence length
- Current service-level tokenization details (if applicable)
- Network topology or egress restrictions (if any)

I've attached a one‑page pre-call checklist and our recommended template for traffic samples.

Thanks — happy to be flexible on timing.

Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172
[Attachment: sizing-precall-checklist.pdf (PDF, 48 KB)]

From: Elena Park <elena.park@aurorapay.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir.rao@aurorapay.com>
Date: 2028-06-15T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: dedicated capacity sizing + next steps

Thanks Jonas — great summary. Samir (head of infra) is on copy and will help gather the traces. We can provide a 72-hour request log and the payload samples you requested.

People to include: Samir Rao (infra), Priya Mehta (platform eng), and myself. We prefer afternoon slots (PDT). Available windows next week:
- Tue 2028-06-20 14:00–15:00 PDT
- Wed 2028-06-21 15:00–16:00 PDT
- Thu 2028-06-22 13:00–14:00 PDT

Two quick clarifications before we lock a time:
1) Do you need VPN access to pull traces, or can we upload artifacts to a temporary S3 bucket?
2) For latency SLOs we expect p95 < 200ms and p99 < 450ms in production — is that within the realistic envelope for your Dedicated offering at preliminary glance?

We'll upload the artifacts to an S3 link and share creds just before the call. Also attaching a network sketch — it's a small PNG so I'll include that in the next email.

Elena
Director of Platform
AuroraPay
elena.park@aurorapay.com | +1 (628) 555-0199
[Attachment: aurorapay-network-diagram.png (PNG, 72 KB)]

Date: 2028-06-15T12:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: dedicated capacity sizing + next steps

Elena — thanks, that timing works. Looping in Sean Gallagher (Solutions Engineer) who will run the technical deep-dive and lead the sizing run.

Sean, quick context: AuroraPay is aiming for p95 < 200ms and p99 < 450ms at peak. They will provide a 72-hour request trace, payload examples, and a short network sketch (attached by Elena). They prefer afternoons PDT next week; Elena listed Tue/Wed/Thu.

Sean — can you take Tue 2028-06-20 14:00 PDT as the primary slot? If that works, I'll send a calendar invite with an S3 upload link and a short pre-call checklist. During the call we'll:
- Validate sample traffic and sequence lengths
- Propose a Dedicated pool configuration (GPU class, pool size) and expected throughput
- Run a quick back-of-envelope cost estimate and a proposed mutual action plan

Jonas

Elena — nice to meet you (virtually). Tue 2028-06-20 14:00 PDT works for me; I’ll reserve a 60-minute deep-dive slot and prepare a short template for the traffic example parsing. A couple of quick operational notes so we can be efficient on the call:

- S3 upload is ideal — please share a pre-signed URL (read-only) or temporary credentials. No VPN required.
- Please include one representative large payload (worst-case token length) and one average-case sample.
- If you have any rate-limited endpoints or bursts that exceed average QPS by >2x, flag those in a readme so we can simulate them.
- If there are on-premise inference hops or strict egress controls, include a short note in the network sketch.

I’ll send the invite momentarily with a Zoom link and a shared Drive folder where we can drop notes. Attached: a 1‑page pre-call checklist and a small parsing script stub we use to normalize timestamps (for their team to run if convenient).

Looking forward to it.

—Sean Gallagher
